title: Collections Account Analyst
description:
The Talent Acquisition department hires qualified candidates to fill positions which contribute to the overall strategic success of Howard University. Hiring staff “for fit” makes significant contributions to Howard University’s overall mission. At Howard University, we prioritize well-being and professional growth.

Here Is What We Offer

  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus mental health support
  • Work-Life Balance: PTO, paid holidays, flexible work arrangements
  • Financial Wellness: Competitive salary, 403(b) with company match
  • Professional Development: Ongoing training, tuition reimbursement, and career advancement paths
  • Additional Perks: Wellness programs, commuter benefits, and a vibrant company culture

Join Howard University and thrive with us!

Basic Function

The Collections Counselor supports students with aging or past-due balances by providing clear, accurate, and compassionate financial guidance. The role conducts proactive outreach, explains payment options, resolves discrepancies, documents activity thoroughly, and collaborates with campus partners to help students regain good financial standing. The position ensures all counseling and communications align with university policies, federal regulations, and service quality standards.

Supervisory Accountability

None

Nature And Scope

The Collections Counselor serves as a frontline financial support specialist within Student Accounts, working directly with students whose balances require follow-up or repayment. The Counselor communicates regularly via phone, email, ticketing, and in-person appointments— occasionally during nontraditional hours—to explain account status, payment plans, holds, and next steps. The role requires strong communication skills, customer-service orientation, attention to detail, and the ability to support adult and traditional learners navigating financial challenges. The incumbent works closely with Collections Leads, Student Accounts Advisors, Cashiering Services, Financial Aid, the Registrar’s Office, Treasury, and other campus partners to resolve discrepancies, verify adjustments, and support the timely and accurate processing of payments. The Counselor reinforces university expectations while maintaining a student-centered, empathetic approach.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Conduct outreach to students with past-due balances to explain account status, payment requirements, repayment options, and consequences of nonpayment.
  • Provide empathetic, student-centered counseling on payment plans, outstanding charges, financial holds, and available resources.
  • Assist students with setting up, monitoring, and understanding payment plan terms, deadlines, and consequences for missed payments.
  • Conduct thorough account reviews, identify discrepancies, and escalate complex or unusual cases to the Collections Lead.
  • Process returned payments, verify financial adjustments, and coordinate with Financial Aid, Registrar, and Cashiering to ensure accurate account updates.
  • Maintain detailed documentation of all outreach, counseling sessions, follow-up actions, and resolutions in accordance with departmental policy.
  • Ensure compliance with FERPA, FDCPA, institutional procedures, and established scripts and communication standards.
  • Prepare routine reports and status updates to support monitoring of aging balances and collection activities.
  • Provide high-quality, professional customer service and reinforce university policy while helping students work toward financial stability.

Core Competencies

  • Demonstrates empathy, patience, and clarity when helping students in financial distress.
  • Accurately interprets account activity and identifies appropriate next steps.
  • Communicates clearly and concisely across phone, email, ticketing, and in-person interactions.
  • Works collaboratively with cross-campus partners to resolve issues efficiently.
  • Maintains accuracy in account reviews, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and supporting evening or nontraditional service hours.
  • Understands billing, collections, payment plan structures, financial aid interactions, and registration impacts.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred; an equivalent combination of education and related experience may be considered.
  • Basic understanding of accounts receivable processess.
  • One to two years of experience in customer service, billing, student accounts, accounts receivable, financial aid, or another financial operations role.
  • Experience supporting adult learners or students facing financial hardship preferred.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain financial concepts clearly and empathetically.
  • Ability to handle confidential information and comply with FERPA, FDCPA, and institutional guidelines.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze account data, identify discrepancies, and elevate complex issues appropriately.
  • Experience with ERP or student information systems (Workday preferred; training provided).
  • Proven ability to manage multiple cases, deadlines, and follow‑up tasks in a high‑volume environment.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Financial Aid, Cashiering, Registrar, Treasury, and other campus partners.

Compliance Salary Range Disclosure

Expected Salary Range: $63,000 - $70,000

title: Project Management Support - Senior Associate
description:
Job Highlight

PT - Standar TDR Clasificado

Esta vaga tem como objetivo identificar um grupo de candidatos a Project Management Support Senior Associate para projetos existentes e futuros no Brasil.

PORTFÓLIO ATUAL: O portfólio do Brasil atualmente implementa 17 projetos – 13 projetos de infraestrutura que variam de baixa, média e alta complexidade, bem como 4 projetos que gerenciam logística para ajuda humanitária, iniciativas de desenvolvimento social e parcerias público-privadas. Os projetos existentes incluem a prestação de apoio ao Fundo Nacional de Desenvolvimento da Educação na finalização da construção de escolas para comunidades indígenas e tradicionais; a gestão da implementação da compensação por dano moral coletivo para bairros afetados por subsidência de mineração em Maceió; o apoio ao Ministério das Cidades na elaboração de 120 planos municipais de redução de risco de desastres (apenas consultoria); e a conclusão da Etapa 1 do Campus da Universidade Federal da Integração Latino-Americana (UNILA) em Foz do Iguaçu; entre outros. Esses projetos, e outros semelhantes no pipeline, são implementados em estreita colaboração com o doador e/ou beneficiários, e variam em complexidade, escopo e valor, de US$ 4 milhões a US$ 150 milhões.

PIPELINE – INSTALAÇÕES INSTITUCIONAIS: O pipeline atual inclui oportunidades para gerenciar o design e/ou a construção e supervisão de instalações institucionais — como edifícios de escritórios públicos, hospital, museu, escolas e projetos de água e saneamento — localizadas em Brasília, Foz do Iguaçu, São Paulo, Pará e outras localidades em todo o Brasil.

Apoiar o sucesso dos projetos por meio de suporte contínuo e excelência operacional.

EN - Standar TDR Clasificado

This vacancy aims to identify a pool of Project Management Support Senior Associate candidates for existing and future projects in Brazil.

CURRENT PORTFOLIO: The Brazil portfolio currently implements 17 projects - 13 infrastructure projects ranging from low, medium and high complexity, as well as 4 projects that manage logistics for humanitarian aid, social development initiatives, and private-public partnerships. Existing projects include the provision of support to the National Education Development Fund in finalizing the construction of schools for indigenous and traditional communities; Managing the implementation of collective moral damage compensation for neighborhoods affected by mining subsidence in Maceio, supporting the Ministry of Cities in preparing 120 municipal disaster risk reduction plans(advisory only); and concluding Stage 1 of the Campus of the Federal University for Latin American Integration (UNILA) in Foz do Iguaçu; among others. These Projects, and others similar in pipeline, are implemented in close collaboration with the donor and/or beneficiaries, and range in complexity, scope and price from $4 million to $150 million.

PIPELINE - INSTITUTIONAL FACILITIES: The current pipeline includes opportunities to manage the design, and/or construction and supervision of institutional facilities—such as public office buildings, hospital, museum, schools, and water and sanitation projects —located in Brasília, Foz do Iguaçu, São Paulo, Pará, and other locations across Brazil.

Supporting project success through seamless support and operational excellence.

Role Purpose

PT

O Project Management Support Senior Associate fornece apoio técnico, administrativo e logístico para garantir a entrega eficiente e eficaz das operações do projeto. O titular do cargo contribui para a coordenação e execução dos processos cotidianos de gestão de projetos, assegurando a conformidade com os padrões e procedimentos do UNOPS. A função é focada no parceiro e orientada a resultados no apoio à implementação oportuna dos projetos.

EN

The Project Management Support Senior Associate provides technical, administrative and logistical support to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of project operations. The incumbent contributes to the coordination and execution of day-to-day project management processes, ensuring compliance with UNOPS standards and procedures. The role is stakeholder-focused and results-oriented in supporting timely project implementation.

Functions / Key Results Expected

PT - Standar TDR Clasificado

  • Monitoramento e Relatórios de Projetos
  • Apoiar o supervisor no monitoramento da implementação do projeto e do desempenho financeiro para garantir a conformidade com as regras, regulamentos e padrões de relatórios do UNOPS.
  • Preparar e manter relatórios de desembolso financeiro e atualizações de progresso em coordenação com Finanças e unidades relevantes.
  • Manter documentação abrangente do projeto, incluindo registros financeiros, arquivos de auditoria e lançamentos no Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) (oneUNOPS), garantindo precisão e integridade.
  • Acompanhar orçamentos do projeto, fluxo de caixa e despesas. Identificar variações, propor revisões orçamentárias e iniciar ações corretivas quando necessário.
  • Registrar dados e atualizações do projeto em logs e registros relevantes, garantindo a precisão das informações para relatórios e auditorias.
  • Elaborar atas de reuniões, acompanhar pontos de ação e auxiliar na compilação de relatórios periódicos de desempenho do projeto e relatórios de encerramento.
  • Apoio à Implementação e Entrega de Projetos
  • Auxiliar na execução cotidiana do projeto, garantindo a adesão às metodologias de gestão de projetos do UNOPS, às regulamentações financeiras e aos padrões de qualidade.
  • Apoiar a preparação, alteração e monitoramento de planos de trabalho do projeto, acordos e revisões orçamentárias.
  • Facilitar a comunicação entre parceiros, prestadores de serviços e equipes internas para garantir a entrega oportuna das atividades do projeto.
  • Acompanhar marcos do projeto, riscos e questões, mantendo registros atualizados e auxiliando no planejamento de mitigação.
  • Apoiar a preparação e revisão de faturas de contratados, a verificação de documentos comprobatórios e a coordenação das entregas.
  • Contribuir para a identificação de gargalos operacionais ou administrativos e propor soluções práticas para aumentar a eficiência do projeto.
  • Apoio Operacional e Administrativo
  • Fornecer assistência administrativa nas operações do projeto, incluindo coordenação de RH, planejamento de aquisições e arranjos logísticos.
  • Apoiar a preparação de Terms of Reference (ToRs), contratos e ordens de compra. Revisar a documentação de suporte antes do envio para aprovação.
  • Coordenar e organizar workshops, treinamentos, reuniões e missões, garantindo arranjos logísticos, financeiros e de viagem oportunos.
  • Articular-se com as unidades de Finanças, RH e Aquisições para processar pagamentos, monitorar compromissos e garantir a conformidade com os sistemas de controle interno.
  • Manter a correspondência, os registros e os sistemas de arquivamento do projeto de acordo com as políticas de gestão documental do UNOPS.
  • Apoiar os processos de integração, indução e gestão de contratos para o pessoal do projeto e consultores.
  • Gestão Financeira e de Aquisições
  • Auxiliar na preparação de orçamentos do projeto, previsões e relatórios de despesas, garantindo precisão e envio oportuno.
  • Monitorar transações financeiras, desembolsos e pagamentos a fornecedores em conformidade com as Regras e Regulamentos Financeiros do UNOPS.
  • Revisar e reconciliar contas do projeto, garantindo que as despesas estejam alinhadas com os orçamentos aprovados e planos de trabalho.
  • Coordenar processos de aquisição, incluindo a preparação de requisições, apoio à avaliação e acompanhamento de contratos e ordens de compra.
  • Facilitar a comunicação com fornecedores, gerenciar a documentação para atividades de aquisição e financeiras e garantir a entrega oportuna dos serviços.
  • Apoiar auditorias do projeto mantendo documentação financeira completa e auxiliando na implementação das recomendações de auditoria.
  • Construção e Compartilhamento de Conhecimento
  • Apoiar a organização, facilitação e realização de treinamentos e sessões de aprendizagem em gestão de projetos.
  • Participar de iniciativas de compartilhamento de conhecimento e Comunidades de Prática (CoPs), contribuindo com insights e lições aprendidas.
  • Realizar pesquisas sobre temas relacionados à gestão de projetos e contribuir para a elaboração de relatórios, resumos e notas informativas.

EN - Standar TDR Clasificado

  • Project Monitoring and Reporting
  • Support the supervisor in monitoring project implementation and financial performance to ensure compliance with UNOPS rules, regulations and reporting standards.
  • Prepare and maintain financial disbursement reports and progress updates in coordination with Finance and relevant units.
  • Maintain comprehensive project documentation, including financial records, audit files and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) entries (oneUNOPS), ensuring accuracy and completeness.
  • Track project budgets, cash flow and expenditures. Identify variances, propose budget revisions, and initiate corrective actions when necessary.
  • Record project data and updates in relevant logs and registers, ensuring information accuracy for reporting and audits.
  • Take minutes of meetings, track action points, and assist in compiling periodic project performance reports and completion reports
  • Project Implementation and Delivery Support
  • Assist in day-to-day project execution, ensuring adherence to UNOPS project management methodologies, financial regulations and quality standards.
  • Support the preparation, amendment, and monitoring of project work plans, agreements and budget revisions.
  • Facilitate communication between partners, service providers and internal teams to ensure the timely delivery of project activities.
  • Track project milestones, risks and issues, maintaining updated records and assisting with mitigation planning.
  • Support preparation and review of contractors’ invoices, verification of supporting documents, and coordination of deliverables.
  • Contribute to identifying operational or administrative bottlenecks and propose practical solutions to enhance project efficiency.
  • Operational and Administrative Support
  • Provide administrative assistance in project operations, including HR coordination, procurement planning and logistical arrangements.
  • Support the preparation of Terms of Reference (ToRs), contracts and purchase orders. Review supporting documentation before submission for approval.
  • Coordinate and organize workshops, trainings, meetings and missions, ensuring timely logistical, financial and travel arrangements.
  • Liaise with Finance, HR and Procurement units to process payments, monitor commitments, and ensure compliance with internal control systems.
  • Maintain project correspondence, records and filing systems in accordance with UNOPS document management policies.
  • Support onboarding, induction, and contract management processes for project personnel and consultants.
  • Financial and Procurement Management
  • Assist in the preparation of project budgets, forecasts, and expenditure reports, ensuring accuracy and timely submission.
  • Monitor financial transactions, disbursements, and vendor payments in alignment with UNOPS Financial Rules and Regulations.
  • Review and reconcile project accounts, ensuring that expenditures align with approved budgets and work plans.
  • Coordinate procurement processes, including requisition preparation, evaluation support, and tracking of contracts and purchase orders.
  • Facilitate communication with vendors, manage documentation for procurement and financial activities, and ensure timely service delivery.
  • Support project audits by maintaining complete financial documentation and assisting in implementing audit recommendations.
  • Knowledge Building and Sharing
  • Support the organization, facilitation and delivery of training and learning sessions on project management.
  • Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and Communities of Practice (CoPs), contributing insights and lessons learned.
  • Conduct research on project management-related topics and contribute to the drafting of reports, summaries and briefing notes

Education Requirements

PT -

Obrigatório
  • Ensino médio (ou equivalente) com 7 anos de experiência relevante OU diploma de bacharelado (ou equivalente) em qualquer área, com 3 anos de experiência relevante, é obrigatório.
Desejável
  • Certificado profissional reconhecido globalmente ou filiação em Gestão de Projetos é desejável.

EN -

Required
  • Secondary school (or equivalent) with 7 years of relevant experience OR Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in any discipline with 3 years of relevant experience is required.
Desired
  • A globally recognized professional certificate or membership in Project Management is desired.

Experience Requirements

PT

Obrigatório
  • Experiência relevante é trabalho em gestão de projetos ou áreas relacionadas.
  • Proficiência demonstrável no uso de ferramentas de colaboração e produtividade (por exemplo, MS Office, G-Suite, etc.) e sistemas de gestão baseados na web é obrigatória.
Desejável
  • Experiência de trabalho em ambientes multiculturais ou em organizações do sistema ONU em um país em desenvolvimento é desejável.
  • Experiência em contextos de desenvolvimento ou humanitários é desejável.

EN

Required
  • Relevant experience is work in project management or related areas.
  • Demonstrable proficiency in the use of collaboration and productivity tools (e.g. MS Office, G-Suite, etc) and web-based management systems are required.
Desired
  • Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired.
  • Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired.

Por que trabalhar conosco?

Porque somos a empresa líder no setor privado de saneamento básico no Brasil. About Us

SBM Offshore is the world’s deepwater ocean‑infrastructure expert. Our work is already resulting in cleaner, more efficient energy production. True. Blue. Transition. is our promise to enable that into the future while at the same time using our expertise to support new and existing markets in the blue economy. While Pioneering More: helping to enable the energy transition and using our unique capabilities in ocean infrastructure to support more industries to grow sustainably. Sharing our experience for a better blue tomorrow.

Purpose

  • As Operations Technical Autority, you provide Regional Ownership and accountability of fleet Safety and Environmentally Critical Element (SECE) Performance Standards within their discipline.
  • You act as part of the local Technical Team in assuring the status of the SECE within your scope.

Responsibilities

  • You travel to all units within your scope at least twice a year to maintain a strong connection with front‑line operations.
  • You provide independent technical advice to regional personnel, ensuring clarity and confidence in operational decisions.
  • You act as the technical liaison between your discipline, the Operations Risk Team, and subject‑matter experts.
  • You contribute your expertise to local SBM initiatives, enhancing safety and operational excellence.
  • You support Major Accident Hazards (MAH) risk management by participating in Operational Risk Assessments and ensuring alignment with company standards.
  • You accept and oversee Operations Performance Standards for your discipline, reviewing and endorsing proposed changes before escalating to the Global OTA (OTA2).
  • You evaluate and approve changes to tag lists and assurance EMS tasks during project phases, ensuring alignment with assurance requirements.
  • You review and endorse Execute Phase Assurance Reports developed by R3 Process Safety Engineers for new units.
  • You approve updates to EMS and Safety and Environmentally Critical Element (SECE) tag lists as requested by Reliability Leads, ensuring compliance with guidelines from the Global OTA.
  • You monitor KPIs for barrier health in your discipline and elevate concerns to Operations Management.
  • You conduct periodic document reviews to ensure SECE performance and barrier strategies align with the unit's Safety Case.
  • You oversee MAH Risk Assessment and Safety Case Reviews for Brownfield Modifications or Life‑Extension Projects.
  • You elevate significant findings from verification and assurance processes to ensure appropriate action is taken.
  • You prepare an annual report on Barrier/SECE management status and the effectiveness of Verification and Assurance Schemes for OTA2 and Regional Operations Management.

  • Minimum Bachelors degree within the discipline for which you are an authority.

Experience

  • Solid experience in technical or engineering roles.
  • Solid experience within an operations setting.

Management of change application

Safety and environmental critical elements

title: Senior Manager, Ocean Policy
description:
Conservation International protects nature for the benefit of humanity. Through science, policy, fieldwork, and finance, we spotlight and secure the most important places in nature for the climate, biodiversity, and for people. With offices in 30 countries and projects in more than 100 countries, Conservation International partners with governments, companies, civil society, Indigenous peoples, and local communities to help people and nature thrive together.

POSITION SUMMARY

This position is open for consideration in the following locations in the Americas, with preference for candidates based in time zones that can accommodate calls with colleagues in Europe and Africa: Arlington-US, Brazil(remote), Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guyana, Mexico, Suriname, Peru

Over the last 10 years, CI has developed a comprehensive Blue Climate program spanning over 20 countries dedicated to identifying and addressing science and policy priorities for oceans and climate globally. The Blue Climate program within the Center for Oceans at CI works closely with our field programs across the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa to design and implement innovative approaches to (1) implement nature-based climate adaptation solutions that improve coastal and marine communities’ livelihoods and resilience while also conserving ecosystems and biodiversity; and (2) conserve and restore coastal blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, salt marshes, and seagrass meadows) for climate change mitigation. The Blue Climate program also has key leadership roles in advancing climate mitigation and adaptation priorities into national and regional coastal management and science through the International Blue Carbon Institute, Blue Carbon Initiative, the International Partnership for Blue Carbon, the Global Mangrove Alliance and the Global Green-Gray Community of Practice, and policy with the Center for Policy and Incentives.

Under the supervision of the Director, Ocean Policy, the Senior Manager, Ocean Policy, is a self‑motivated, creative team member integral to the long‑term growth and success of CI’s Blue Climate program and Ocean Policy team. The Senior Manager, Ocean Policy will support the development, implementation and management of strategic international policy‑based approaches and programs to achieve CI’s Ocean Policy goals spanning coastal resilience, climate mitigation, green‑gray infrastructure, blue carbon ecosystems and ocean‑climate integration. Together with the Director, Ocean Policy, they will work with CI’s Center for Policy and Incentives to ensure alignment with CI’s larger international and national policy programs and priorities, including providing technical inputs and guidance on ocean‑climate issues. The position will also work closely with teams across CI including other programs within the Center for Oceans and the Moore Center for Science and Solutions to ensure alignment and integration of ocean policy priorities with all related CI programs and topic areas, including biodiversity, finance, and community fisheries.

Responsibilities

International Ocean Policy

  • Manage strategic policy initiatives to achieve CI’s Ocean Policy goals spanning coastal resilience, green‑gray infrastructure, blue carbon, and other ocean‑climate areas which integrate and align international and national policy goals.
  • Work closely with CI’s Center for Policy and Incentives to ensure ocean‑climate strategies and approaches are aligned with international and national policy programs and priorities.
  • Play a key role in project development, fundraising, implementation, communications, and broader capacity building for the Ocean Policy program.
  • Contribute to the drafting and revision of CI ocean policy positions, policy briefs, guidance documents, and other technical resources.
  • Play a key role in representing the Center for Oceans within the CI delegation to international policy meetings related to climate, biodiversity, and oceans, such as the UNFCCC climate COP and intersessional meetings. title: Security Specialist - Penetration Tester & Hardening Specialist
description:
Who Are We?

Decentralized Masters is at the forefront of DeFi education globally. In just two years, we have grown from a pioneering pair of co‑founders to over 140 dedicated professionals. Today, we are recognized as one of the fastest‑growing enterprises in the sector, with industry insiders predicting our evolution into a unicorn company by 2030. Operating on a bootstrapped model, we are on track to achieve an impressive $50 million in revenue this year alone.

Our Impact

While our growth has been remarkable, we take even greater pride in the success of our clients. To date, we have empowered over 4,000 investors to break into the DeFi world. At Decentralized Masters, we don’t just offer education; we cultivate a powerhouse of knowledge combined with an engaging community, innovative technology, and a team of leading DeFi and blockchain experts. Our commitment is to deliver unparalleled resources designed for long‑term success in the world of DeFi and Web3, ensuring our members not only safeguard but also enhance their financial future.

Our Vision

Our goal is to create the largest and most influential DeFi ecosystem the world has ever seen, starting with becoming the gold standard in DeFi education. This vision is ambitious, transformative, and poised to change the landscape of digital finance.

Are You Ready?

This is more than just a job; it’s an opportunity to shape the future of Web3 technology and education. Are you ready to be part of our vision to redefine what’s possible in DeFi and beyond? Apply below, and let’s explore this journey together.

Check us out here:

What will you be doing?

We’re looking for a hungry, junior security professional whose default instinct is to attack first, patch second. This isn’t a governance‑and‑policy desk job. You’ll spend your days trying to break into our own systems, finding the cracks before anyone else does, and then relentlessly closing them.

If your idea of a good day is discovering a misconfigured S3 bucket, popping a shell on a test environment, and writing up the fix before lunch, read on.

Break things (on purpose)

  • Continuously run penetration tests against our web apps, APIs, internal tools, and cloud infrastructure
  • Conduct phishing simulations and social engineering tests against our own team
  • Perform recon, enumeration, and exploitation attempts on our systems in a controlled, authorized way
  • Hunt for vulnerabilities before real attackers do – then document and escalate them

Harden everything you find

  • Work directly with engineering to remediate vulnerabilities you uncover
  • Tighten cloud security configurations (AWS) – IAM policies, exposed services, secrets management
  • Review access controls and flag over‑privileged accounts, then drive least‑privilege fixes
  • Implement and tune monitoring tools (SIEM, IDS/IPS) so we catch anything that slips through

Keep the lights on

  • Assist with incident detection and response when real events occur
  • Help maintain audit logs and ensure we have visibility across our systems
  • Support compliance work (GDPR, SOC 2) as it relates to technical controls

Requirements – What You Will Bring

Must‑have

  • 1–2 years of experience in security, pentesting, bug bounty, or a related hands‑on role (or equivalent self‑taught experience with proof)
  • Demonstrable ability to find and exploit common vulnerabilities – OWASP‑Top 10, misconfigurations, broken access controls
  • Basic cloud security knowledge (AWS preferred) – you know what "public S3 bucket" means and why it’s bad
  • Comfortable using tools like Burp Suite, Nmap, Metasploit, or similar
  • Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and how to think like a threat actor
  • You document your findings clearly – written reports matter as much as the exploit

Nice‑to‑have

  • CTF experience or an active HackTheBox / TryHackMe profile
  • Any security certifications: eJPT, CEH, Security+, OSCP (in progress counts)
  • Scripting ability in Python or Bash to automate recon or testing
  • Interest or background in DeFi, crypto, or Web3 security
  • Familiarity with smart contract attack vectors (a big bonus)

Benefits – What We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Fully remote – work from anywhere
  • Unlimited PTO and flexible schedule
  • Team off‑sites and events
  • A genuine mandate to break our stuff and make us stronger for it

Ready to hack with purpose? If you’ve been sharpening your skills on bug bounties, CTFs, or homelab environments and want your first real shot at doing this professionally, we want to hear from you. Show us what you’ve found, what you’ve broken, and how you fixed it.

title: Director, School Counseling and University Admissions
description:
Want to revolutionize the future of education and do meaningful work that transforms future generations’ lives? Our team is looking to bring on passionate educators to support our growing student base through part‑time teaching roles. This position offers the opportunity to teach bright, motivated students from around the world while maintaining flexibility in your schedule. You’ll play a key role in delivering high‑quality, personalized learning experiences as we continue to expand our reach globally.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Director of School Counseling and University Admissions to serve as a critical bridge between our A‑level and US curriculum pathways. This role combines strategic leadership with hands‑on student counseling to ensure every CGA student receives world‑class university guidance while building scalable systems that maintain excellence as we grow. The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in both US and UK education systems, demonstrated success in placing students in top universities globally, and the vision to create comprehensive programs that develop future‑ready students. This role requires someone who can work directly with students requiring personalized counseling while simultaneously building the infrastructure, playbooks, and training materials that enable consistent counseling quality across our global team.

Purpose

Support students across both curriculum pathways (A‑level and US) to help ensure a unified approach to setting students up for success and consistency of practice for academic excellence. This role acts as a bridge between the two curriculum pathways, ensuring that students have the support they need to choose the path that best aligns with their future goals. You’ll provide hands‑on student counseling support for top universities, support clubs, create enrichment programs, and build scalable systems to ensure students arrive at the application stage well‑prepared with strong academic foundations, examination results, rich extracurricular profiles, global competencies in real‑world experiences, and clear university pathways aligned to personal goals and CGA’s institutional strengths.

Key Responsibilities

Cross‑Pathway Leadership & Coordination

  • Facilitate knowledge sharing and best practice exchange between campuses and across curriculum types (A‑level and US pathways)
  • Collaborate with academic staff, admissions teams, and deans to align curricular offerings with student outcomes and market demand
  • Monitor and benchmark academic performance across campuses and curricula to drive continuous improvement
  • Ensure consistency of practice for academic excellence across both curriculum pathways
  • Work as part of an extended team across time zones to support our global nature

Examination Management & Academic Performance

  • Support examination management across A‑levels, AP, and SAT programs
  • Develop and oversee comprehensive exam preparation programs across all curricula
  • Implement data‑driven strategies to improve student outcomes
  • Support accreditation and compliance for institutional relationships

Academic Enrichment & Future‑Ready Student Development

  • Create programs that develop globally competitive students prepared for the future of work
  • Support and coordinate academic competitions to build student competitiveness
  • Develop real‑world experiences and vibrant community connections for students
  • Support student clubs and enrichment programs
  • Ensure students develop strong academic foundations, rich extracurricular profiles, and global competencies
  • Build connections between students and opportunities that develop future‑ready skills

Clubs & Extracurricular Programs

  • Design and implement a comprehensive club structure and system across CGA that ensures consistency and quality
  • Support student clubs and organizations to foster community connection in a virtual environment
  • Create frameworks and guidelines for club formation, leadership, and sustainability
  • Develop and maintain a diverse portfolio of extracurricular opportunities aligned with university admissions expectations
  • Ensure student leadership development through club participation and officer roles
  • Monitor club engagement and participation to identify opportunities for student connection
  • Build partnerships with external organizations to provide authentic extracurricular experiences
  • Track and document student extracurricular involvement for university applications
  • Create virtual and asynchronous club opportunities that accommodate students across time zones

Direct University Admissions Counseling

  • Deliver world‑class university admissions counseling through direct student support
  • Work directly with a select cohort of high‑intensity students requiring comprehensive personalized counseling
  • Provide strategic planning for university applications, including subject selection and pathway decisions
  • Manage predicted grades and letters of recommendation for students
  • Guide students through UCAS, Common App, and country‑specific application systems
  • Ensure students meet all deadlines across multiple application systems globally
  • Review and provide feedback on personal statements, essays, and supplemental materials
  • Provide comprehensive guidance on university selection across US, UK, Canadian, European, Australian, Asian, and other international systems
  • Coordinate financial aid and scholarship applications with families
  • Maintain current knowledge of admissions requirements, deadlines, and trends across global universities

Building Scalable Systems & Infrastructure

  • Build scalable systems that ensure all CGA students receive expert guidance through their application process
  • Create comprehensive counseling playbooks and frameworks for counselors and deans to follow
  • Develop standardized processes for predicted grades, recommendation letters, and application quality assurance
  • Build training materials and resources to establish consistent counseling quality across the team
  • Establish quality standards and benchmarks for university counseling
  • Design asynchronous resources supporting part‑time students through their application journeys
  • Develop and maintain an extensive database of university programs, scholarships, and requirements globally
  • Build systems that can evolve as our school grows

Data & Performance Tracking

  • Support data dashboards tracking application progress and outcomes for areas of improvement
  • Ensure data is transparent and reportable across all school leadership
  • Track and analyze university admissions outcomes to inform program improvements
  • Generate reports on student outcomes and program metrics
  • Use data to identify trends and optimize counseling strategies

Strategic Partnerships & Market Intelligence

  • Monitor global education and admissions trends to adjust CGA's approach and maintain competitive advantage
  • Cultivate relationships with university admissions offices to enhance CGA's institutional reputation
  • Build partnerships with universities to create opportunities for CGA students
  • Represent CGA at virtual university fairs and recruitment events
  • Stay informed about test‑optional policies, holistic admissions trends, and evolving university requirements

Student Support & Academic Advising

  • Advise students on course rigor, AP subject selection, A‑level subject combinations, prerequisites, and graduation requirements
  • Provide counseling to address academic stress, time management, and study skills
  • Support students navigating the unique challenges of online learning
  • Serve as an advocate for student needs within the school community
  • Coordinate with families through virtual information sessions and regular communication
  • Create learning environments where every student discovers and develops their unique strengths

Administrative & Compliance

  • Maintain accurate student records and university application tracking systems
  • Prepare school reports, transcripts, and counselor recommendation letters
  • Collaborate with school leadership on policy development and strategic planning

Leadership Values & Approach

  • Unlock Potential Together: We work collaboratively. No team is an island. Adapt quickly and find solutions that are in the best interests of our families and CGA as a whole. Every student is a VIP. Make decisive actions to propel us forward through a lens of optimism.
  • Rethink, Rebuild: Avoid defaulting to, “We’ve always done this.” Be curious, look outside your sphere of inspiration, and dive into the data for actionable insights. Online is our advantage. Let’s make the most of the innovation at our fingertips. Take immediate action to improve always, take accountability, follow through, and get ready to optimize again.
  • Raise the bar, compound impact: Continually strive to be better tomorrow. Have high standards for yourself and those around you. Tackle hard things with grit, take your work seriously, but not yourself. Take the time to document work, proactively share learnings, and multiply others’ efforts. Give credit to those making a positive impact.

Qualifications

Education & Credentials

  • Master’s degree in School Counseling, Guidance Counseling, Higher Education, or related field
  • Valid school counseling credential/license (or equivalent from home country)
  • Demonstrable expertise in both US and UK education systems

Experience

  • Minimum 5-7 years of experience in high school college counseling or university admissions
  • Proven track record of successfully placing students in competitive universities globally
  • Experience building scalable systems, frameworks, or programs in an educational setting
  • Experience working with international students or in an international school setting
  • Demonstrated knowledge of university admissions processes in multiple countries (US, UK, Canada, Europe, Asia, Australia)
  • Deep experience with both AP and A‑level curriculum pathways
  • Familiarity with online/virtual education delivery
  • Experience with data analysis and using metrics to drive program improvement

Knowledge & Skills

  • Expert knowledge of US university admissions (Common App, Coalition App, UC system, liberal arts colleges, Ivy League)
  • Expert knowledge of UK university admissions (UCAS, Russell Group, requirements for Oxbridge)
  • Working knowledge of university systems in Canada, Australia, Europe, and Asia
  • Understanding of international baccalaureate equivalencies and credit transfers
  • Proficiency with student information systems and college planning software (Naviance, Scoir, Cialfo, or similar)
  • Strong knowledge of scholarship and financial aid resources globally
  • Familiarity with FERPA, GDPR, and educational privacy laws
  • Ability to develop training materials, playbooks, and scalable processes

Technical & Communication Skills

  • Excellent virtual communication and presentation skills
  • Proficiency with video conferencing platforms (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams)
  • Strong written communication skills for emails, reports, recommendation letters, and counseling materials
  • Ability to use learning management systems and collaboration tools
  • Digital literacy and comfort with educational technology
  • Experience with data visualization and dashboard creation for tracking outcomes
